title: Propose safe multi-machine Engram use for Greg's decision, with options and estimates
outcome: Propose safe multi-machine Engram use for Greg's decision, with options and estimates
acceptance: A written proposal covers the intended user workflow, the active-writer model, offline and conflict behaviour, the separation of transport from backup, migration implications for live stores, validation, and rollout

It presents at least two concrete options (including the V9 sequential portable handoff, and how a read-only view on a second machine replaces the removed Beads fallback, or why it is not offered), each with risks and an effort estimate in implementation items
Both architects record concurrence or a stated dissent on the options, and the proposal reaches Greg through Engram::Advisor for his decision; no implementation starts before that decision

Every option, its acceptance criteria and its rollout plan keep sync explicitly configurable and optional: with no remote configured the local-first store is fully functional with no background network activity; enabling sync, choosing the remote, and each push or pull are deliberate visible user actions; disabling sync leaves the local store usable
